title: Uppercase Used at Beginning of Paragraph

illustrates.quote: Follow print for capitalization at the beginning of a paragraph.

blocks.text: THE OLD WOMAN FOLLOWED THEM home from the grocery store.
blocks.features: Opening words 'THE OLD WOMAN FOLLOWED THEM' set in full capitals (a stylistic/decorative print opening); the remainder ('home from the grocery store.') is in ordinary sentence case.

braille.notes: Two lines, verbatim, no line number shown in the source. The triple capital-word indicator ',,,' before the capitalised run preserves the print's full-capitals opening; the remainder is in ordinary case, per rule 1.9.1 ('follow print for capitalization').

resolution: Both runs agree on wording and braille content; the only difference was descriptive-prose phrasing (merged here). Representable: a single 'para' block with the literal capitalization from print, translated by Emboss's own liblouis UEB table (no Emboss-authored capitalisation logic is involved, per F-68's own point about foreign/contraction handling being liblouis's responsibility -- capitalisation indicators are likewise a liblouis translation matter, not an Emboss format-layer feature).
